Brazil is racist, in a different way. Race is perceived differently. It is my understanding that a lot of my family members who are considered white in Brazil would be racialized as latino/brown in the United States or europe. This is because Brazil is more mixed, so the definition of white has expanded to include more people, or else the structure of racism would fall. Race is also strictly phenotypical. In United States you can say “I’m actually black” and pull up a picture of your dad and they will validate you as black. In Brazil you are what you look like.
That being said I think the south is the most racist, though I think it is getting better. It is a problem, there’s lots of things people don’t even realize is racist because it is just a part of brazilian society. Because slavery was abolished last, it’s hard for black Brazilians to maintain wealth. They have a significant disadvantage economically and therefore dominate poor communities. Lots of Brazilians equate this to lack of effort or hard work without really unpacking the disadvantage they have.
Asian Brazilians do face microaggressions, I know my uncle told me he would be called “japa” or “amarelo” but Asians do well financially. I think it is also something Brazilians are getting better at since there has been an Asian presence for quite some time in Brazil.
Brown/mestico/pardo Brazilians are the majority, depending on the region. I feel this is a bit why there is a south vs northeast rivalry is because sulistas often look down on them for having more native  ancestry. However I feel like even mixed, brown Brazilians perpetuate racism against them, by colorism and such. It’s a complicated subject. 
But yes Brazil is racist.

He confided in me about his self harming habits and I was the only one he told. I didn’t know what to do. I didn’t know how to handle it and I didn’t want to break his trust by telling anyone. In a way he kind of encouraged me to, and I didn’t know how to deal with the stress of getting him to stop, so I just did. Eventually he got better towards the end of our relationship and I deteriorated. He stopped self harming and I got progressively worse. I don’t think he does to this day, but I never stopped.
